Channels

6
NameKindContract
argvargv-env
{
  "notes": "One long-lived `grok agent leader` plus leader-attached ACP controllers (`grok agent --leader --leader-socket <sock> stdio`) and the native viewer (`grok --leader --leader-socket <sock> --resume <id>`)."
}
acpacp
{
  "notes": "Strict JSON-RPC 2.0 NDJSON over stdio. Standard session/update and the xAI extension methods remain distinct; the leader fans session traffic out to every attached client."
}
session-lognative-log
{
  "notes": "Append-only GROK_HOME/sessions/<encoded cwd>/<session>/updates.jsonl records {timestamp (Unix seconds), method, params}."
}
session-statenative-state
{
  "notes": "Replace-in-place signals.json, summary.json, and usage.json beside updates.jsonl."
}
leaderunix-socket
{
  "notes": "Coordination socket owned by `grok agent leader`; topology, not an event source. On SIGTERM 1.0.70 drains for about 2 s, exits 143, and unlinks the socket; leader.lock remains."
}
terminalterminal
{
  "notes": "Native leader-attached viewer. In 1.0.70 it renders and can answer leader-routed permission requests, including one issued before it attached; the first answer from any client wins. Semantics come from ACP and the durable store, never terminal text."
}

Advertises loadSession, sessionCapabilities {list, resume, close}, mcpCapabilities {http, sse}, and promptCapabilities {image: true (false in 1.0.0), audio: false, embeddedContext: true}; authMethods are [xai.api_key, grok.com]. Grok-specific `_meta` carries the cwd, agentVersion, a stable machine-derived agentId (UUIDv5), a per-process agentInstanceId, hostname, modelState, availableCommands, and feature flags. sessionCapabilities.additionalDirectories is not advertised even though the CLI gained --add-dir.

      "type": "object"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema"
}

{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$defs": {
    "AgentCapabilities": {
      "description": "Capabilities supported by the agent.\n\nAdvertised during initialization to inform the client about\navailable features and content types.\n\nSee protocol docs: [Agent Capabilities](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/initialization#agent-capabilities)",
      "properties": {
        "_meta": {
          "additionalProperties": true,
          "description": "The _meta property is reserved by ACP to allow clients and agents to attach additional\nmetadata to their interactions. Implementations MUST NOT make assumptions about values at\nthese keys.\n\nSee protocol docs: [Extensibility](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/extensibility)",
          "type": [
            "object",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "auth": {
          "allOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/AgentAuthCapabilities"
            }
          ],
          "default": {},
          "description": "**UNSTABLE**\n\nThis capability is not part of the spec yet, and may be removed or changed at any point.\n\nAuthentication-related capabilities supported by the agent."
        },
        "loadSession": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Whether the agent supports `session/load`.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "mcpCapabilities": {
          "allOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/McpCapabilities"
            }
          ],
          "default": {
            "http": false,
            "sse": false
          },
          "description": "MCP capabilities supported by the agent."
        },
        "nes": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/NesCapabilities"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "**UNSTABLE**\n\nThis capability is not part of the spec yet, and may be removed or changed at any point.\n\nNES (Next Edit Suggestions) capabilities supported by the agent."
        },
        "positionEncoding": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/PositionEncodingKind"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "**UNSTABLE**\n\nThis capability is not part of the spec yet, and may be removed or changed at any point.\n\nThe position encoding selected by the agent from the client's supported encodings."
        },
        "promptCapabilities": {
          "allOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/PromptCapabilities"
            }
          ],
          "default": {
            "audio": false,
            "embeddedContext": false,
            "image": false
          },
          "description": "Prompt capabilities supported by the agent."
        },
        "sessionCapabilities": {
          "allOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/SessionCapabilities"
            }
          ],
          "default": {}
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "Implementation": {
      "description": "Metadata about the implementation of the client or agent.\nDescribes the name and version of an MCP implementation, with an optional\ntitle for UI representation.",
      "properties": {
        "_meta": {
          "additionalProperties": true,
          "description": "The _meta property is reserved by ACP to allow clients and agents to attach additional\nmetadata to their interactions. Implementations MUST NOT make assumptions about values at\nthese keys.\n\nSee protocol docs: [Extensibility](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/extensibility)",
          "type": [
            "object",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "name": {
          "description": "Intended for programmatic or logical use, but can be used as a display\nname fallback if title isn’t present.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "title": {
          "description": "Intended for UI and end-user contexts — optimized to be human-readable\nand easily understood.\n\nIf not provided, the name should be used for display.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "version": {
          "description": "Version of the implementation. Can be displayed to the user or used\nfor debugging or metrics purposes. (e.g. \"1.0.0\").",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "name",
        "version"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    "AuthMethod": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "allOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/AuthMethodEnvVar"
            }
          ],
          "description": "**UNSTABLE**\n\nThis capability is not part of the spec yet, and may be removed or changed at any point.\n\nUser provides a key that the client passes to the agent as an environment variable.",
          "properties": {
            "type": {

      "description": "Describes an available authentication method.\n\nThe `type` field acts as the discriminator in the serialized JSON form.\nWhen no `type` is present, the method is treated as `agent`."
    },

      "description": "Protocol version identifier.\n\nThis version is only bumped for breaking changes.\nNon-breaking changes should be introduced via capabilities.",
      "format": "uint16",
      "maximum": 65535,

      "type": "integer"

    "NesCapabilities": {

    "PositionEncodingKind": {
      "description": "The encoding used for character offsets in positions.\n\nFollows the same conventions as LSP 3.17. The default is UTF-16.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "utf-16",
          "description": "Character offsets count UTF-16 code units. This is the default.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "utf-32",
          "description": "Character offsets count Unicode code points.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "utf-8",
          "description": "Character offsets count UTF-8 code units (bytes).",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "PromptCapabilities": {
      "description": "Prompt capabilities supported by the agent in `session/prompt` requests.\n\nBaseline agent functionality requires support for [`ContentBlock::Text`]\nand [`ContentBlock::ResourceLink`] in prompt requests.\n\nOther variants must be explicitly opted in to.\nCapabilities for different types of content in prompt requests.\n\nIndicates which content types beyond the baseline (text and resource links)\nthe agent can process.\n\nSee protocol docs: [Prompt Capabilities](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/initialization#prompt-capabilities)",

          "type": "boolean"

Cancels the running turn: the prompt result reports stopReason cancelled with cancellationCategory MidTurnAbort. A permission request still pending is resolved by the cancel (interaction_resolved, no tool_call_update), and the leader sends its client no $/cancel_request.

Before the result the leader replays history to the loading client as `_x.ai/session/update` and `session/update` frames with `_meta.isReplay: true` and `_meta["x.ai/leaderClientId"]`. The replay is a reconstruction, not a byte copy of updates.jsonl: tool calls replay as `tool_call` only.

{"payload":"exact","result":"sampled","carrier":"structural","limitations":["Exact ACP schema 0.11.4 (v0.11.4, e9313572), the dependency of the nearest public Grok mirror commit. The binary embeds agent-client-protocol-0.10.4 (binary probe), and every captured 1.0.70 carrier validates against it; the schema is not the binary's own source.","The result schema is allOf(exact ACP, sampled Grok 1.0.70 instance): the sampled branch records Grok's observed extension fields. Sampled from the Grok 1.0.70 darwin-arm64 census: observed JSON types per field, with required fields present in every captured instance. Sanitized strings keep their type but not their value, so enumerations and formats are not inferred.","The carrier fixes the JSON-RPC envelope and method; params are validated by the payload schema."]}

The result `_meta` carries promptId, token counters, and (except on MidTurnAbort) a usage object; cancelled turns add cancellationCategory MidTurnAbort | PermissionRejected | PermissionCancelled (a permission prompt cancelled in the viewer) and, for PermissionRejected, cancellationContext {tool_name, reason}. turn_completed and `_x.ai/session/prompt_complete` precede the result; signals.json is rewritten asynchronously after it.

{"payload":"sampled","result":"exact","carrier":"structural","limitations":["Exact ACP schema 0.11.4 (v0.11.4, e9313572), the dependency of the nearest public Grok mirror commit. The binary embeds agent-client-protocol-0.10.4 (binary probe), and every captured 1.0.70 carrier validates against it; the schema is not the binary's own source.","The payload schema is allOf(exact ACP, sampled Grok 1.0.70 instance): the sampled branch records Grok's observed extension fields. Sampled from the Grok 1.0.70 darwin-arm64 census: observed JSON types per field, with required fields present in every captured instance. Sanitized strings keep their type but not their value, so enumerations and formats are not inferred.","The result is written by the ACP client (here the census controller); the exact ACP response schema is its contract.","The carrier fixes the JSON-RPC envelope and method; params are validated by the payload schema."]}

Sent only for tools Grok classes as needing approval: a bare `echo` runs without a request (rawOutput.was_bare_echo), a redirecting command asks. The leader fans the request out to every attached client; the 1.0.70 native viewer renders it too (also one issued before the viewer attached) and the first answer wins. The other client receives only the broadcast interaction_resolved {tool_call_id} (no outcome) and the tool call’s own update: in_progress/completed when allowed, failed with `_meta.toolNotRun` rejected (reject) or cancelled (the viewer prompt cancelled); never a $/cancel_request. A later answer to the resolved request id, whatever its outcome, is ignored (the leader logs "received response for unknown request id"). With remembered approvals enabled (the default) the options are always-allow/allow_always, allow-once/allow_once, reject-once/reject_once, reject-always/reject_always in that order; choosing allow_always — in the viewer too — persists one GROK_HOME/sessions/<cwd>/permission__<controller argv>.toml rule that answers the next matching command without a request (approval probe viewer-answers-always). spawn_subagent requests, and every request with GROK_REMEMBER_TOOL_APPROVALS=0, offer only allow-once/allow_once and reject-once/reject_once.

    "ContentBlock": {
      "description": "Content blocks represent displayable information in the Agent Client Protocol.\n\nThey provide a structured way to handle various types of user-facing content—whether\nit's text from language models, images for analysis, or embedded resources for context.\n\nContent blocks appear in:\n- User prompts sent via `session/prompt`\n- Language model output streamed through `session/update` notifications\n- Progress updates and results from tool calls\n\nThis structure is compatible with the Model Context Protocol (MCP), enabling\nagents to seamlessly forward content from MCP tool outputs without transformation.\n\nSee protocol docs: [Content](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/content)",
      "discriminator": {
        "propertyName": "type"
      },
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "allOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/TextContent"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Text content. May be plain text or formatted with Markdown.\n\nAll agents MUST support text content blocks in prompts.\nClients SHOULD render this text as Markdown.",
          "properties": {
            "type": {
              "const": "text",
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "type"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "allOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/ImageContent"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Images for visual context or analysis.\n\nRequires the `image` prompt capability when included in prompts.",
          "properties": {
            "type": {
              "const": "image",
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "type"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "allOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/AudioContent"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Audio data for transcription or analysis.\n\nRequires the `audio` prompt capability when included in prompts.",
          "properties": {
            "type": {
              "const": "audio",
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "type"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "allOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/ResourceLink"
            }
          ],
          "description": "References to resources that the agent can access.\n\nAll agents MUST support resource links in prompts.",
          "properties": {
            "type": {
              "const": "resource_link",
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "type"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "allOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/EmbeddedResource"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Complete resource contents embedded directly in the message.\n\nPreferred for including context as it avoids extra round-trips.\n\nRequires the `embeddedContext` prompt capability when included in prompts.",
          "properties": {
            "type": {
              "const": "resource",
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "type"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        }
      ]
    },
    "ToolCallContent": {
      "description": "Content produced by a tool call.\n\nTool calls can produce different types of content including\nstandard content blocks (text, images) or file diffs.\n\nSee protocol docs: [Content](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/tool-calls#content)",

      "oneOf": [

    "ToolKind": {
      "description": "Categories of tools that can be invoked.\n\nTool kinds help clients choose appropriate icons and optimize how they\ndisplay tool execution progress.\n\nSee protocol docs: [Creating](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/tool-calls#creating)",

      "description": "A single entry in the execution plan.\n\nRepresents a task or goal that the assistant intends to accomplish\nas part of fulfilling the user's request.\nSee protocol docs: [Plan Entries](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/agent-plan#plan-entries)",
